reason: Selected component and cost analyses support testing fused actions and evaluating whole-task cost, with meaningful quality trade-offs in the efficiency stack.

candidates.title: Expose frequently paired actions through a tested fused interface
candidates.rule: For coding-agent workflows with repeated adjacent actions, compare a fused tool-schema action with the existing separate calls, validating both triggering and task success.
candidates.passage: Every component reduces the total token count under both backends.
candidates.location: Section 3.4, Table 4; Action Fusion case study Section 3.5
candidates.finding: Adding Action Fusion to Pi reduces recorded traffic and cost while raising average EdgeBench score under both tested backends. The recorded lineage reports unreliable prompt-only triggering before exposing the action directly in the tool schema.
candidates.conditions: The add-one test keeps Pi as baseline and changes one selected mechanism. The interface is refined on development tasks before held-out validation.
candidates.limitations: One selected mechanism and benchmark; prompt-versus-schema triggering is a development case study rather than a randomized isolated comparison. No evidence that arbitrary action fusion is safe or improves other workflows.
candidates.validation_test: Identify repeated action pairs from traces; compare separate and fused calls on disjoint tasks, checking intermediate preconditions, invalid calls, token cost and final quality.

candidates.title: Evaluate context compaction by full-task cost and quality
candidates.rule: When tuning context compaction, measure total billed activity and task quality rather than choosing the policy with the highest prompt-cache reuse.
candidates.passage: preserving a long prefix is not always the cheapest choice over an entire task.
candidates.location: Section 3.4, Table 4, Cache Reuse and Total Cost
candidates.finding: The full Sol stack lowers cache-read traffic but raises cache writes and reduces fixed-price model cost. Its average score is below baseline in both backend blocks, so lower cost must be assessed against the quality change.
candidates.conditions: Cost includes recorded input, cache read/write and output under fixed prices; component and full-stack comparisons are available.
candidates.limitations: No universal acceptable quality tolerance is established. Recorded traffic is not the same as uncached token count; search-development costs and price changes matter. Triggered-subset comparisons do not isolate mechanism interactions.
candidates.validation_test: Compare compaction policies on identical tasks with provider-measured costs, latency and quality. Include cache writes and any compaction calls; set the acceptable quality loss before selecting a policy.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
